text:
The schedule showed 80 days of float on one unit. The real figure was 7.

Nothing was wrong with the logic. Float was being measured to the final completion date, while that unit had its own contract key date months earlier.

What I did:
• Put a limit on every interim key date, so float is measured to the date that matters.
• Re-ran the schedule and the DCMA 14-point check.

What changed:
• Median task float in that unit: about 80 days → 7.
• Activities with more than 44 days of float: 250 → 10.
• Negative float: 2 → 0.
• No dates moved. Only the truth about them did.

Comfortable float is easy to approve and hard to deliver.

How do you check that the float in your schedule is real?

#ProjectControls #Planning #PrimaveraP6 #Scheduling #DCMA14 #EPC
